_comment: Task 2.3: the Horns' camp, attached to ruin_surface's `ceria_dig_camp` NPC. A SEPARATE graph file, not nodes inside ceria_intro.json: a graph is one file (game.gd keys dialogue_graphs by basename) and always opens at its own `start`, with no per-entity start-node override, so camp_hub could never be reached through ceria_intro's hub. The split is also what the place-naming validator wants -- the horns_dig GIVER maps stay disjoint from the join_dig PRODUCER map. SPOILER RULE: no line here names a door; the reveal is the pedestal's open_toast. NO door_retrieved arm lives here: the camp survives the whole haul window, so a past-tense arm would be wrong while the haul is still running; spec 8's past-tense arm stays on ceria_intro's hub.

camp_hub.speaker: Ceria
camp_hub.text: You made it. Camp rules: nobody touches anything shiny, nobody wanders past the survey stakes alone. The sealed level's below the pedestal court. We found the site off an old expedition ledger — half the pages are about what they didn't bring out. It's in my tent, filed with the survey maps.

options.text: Who else is on this crew?

camp_fourth._comment: #349 four-member reading, camp side. The option is ungated and openable on a first interact, so it asserts NO observation (the earlier 'fourth bedroll' named `dig_camp_remnant`, out of window here). It agrees with a prop that IS live: `dig_camp_notes` shares the hours out EVEN across four names. SPOILER RULE: no door named.
camp_fourth.speaker: Ceria
camp_fourth.text: Pisces. He's ours. He bills the team by invoice, and the roster carries four names with the hours split four ways. He takes his in the city with a treatise open, which is exactly where I want him until there's something down here worth reading. Three of us hold the shovels. That was the trade, and he argued it well.
